items.title: Chuck Findley interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 6, 2023
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] It does. I think Bill Watrous said you can go out but you better know how to come back in.

ctx.x: player and very nice, and he would come over to the house, I mean he’d be at the house and his friend Lenny Russo was a drummer who I worked with and I used to sit in the back seat with his drums on these gigs when I was fourteen but he’d be there and they’d play the blues. I’ll never forget it. They’d start playing the blues, B flat blues, and my brother says to me, “Play.” I said, “Play what?” He said, “Just play.” So I started playing and when it would go to the four chord if I hit the wrong note on the four…
It does. I think Bill Watrous said you can go out but you better know how to come back in.

Of course. You have to come back to make some sense to it, you don’t want them to leave if you’re playing a live concert, a live performance. You know it’s like, and growing up I played in Cleveland, and I played in this one band it was called, well the club was called — well the club was called Paderewski’s and it was, the family was related to Ignace Paderewski from Poland — the famous composer. And I think he was the minister of something in Poland, Warsaw. But the family was Polish and it was called…
